clips.send: Melting. Solid, liquid (heat is absorbed). Ice melts at 0 degrees Celsius . This is its melting point. While melting, the temperature stays at 0 degrees Celsius until all the ice has melted. The energy breaks the lattice apart. Melting 1 g of ice takes 334 J of energy.
clips.text: Melting. Solid → liquid (heat is absorbed). Ice melts at 0 °C. This is its melting point.. While melting, the temperature stays at 0 °C until all the ice has melted. The energy breaks the lattice apart.. Melting 1 g of ice takes 334 J of energy.

clips.send: Sublimation. Solid, gas, skipping the liquid (heat is absorbed). Particles at the surface of a solid escape straight into the gas. Dry ice (solid carbon dioxide) sublimates at minus 78 degrees Celsius : it never becomes a puddle. Snow can slowly disappear on cold, sunny, dry days without melting.
clips.text: Sublimation. Solid → gas, skipping the liquid (heat is absorbed). Particles at the surface of a solid escape straight into the gas.. Dry ice (solid carbon dioxide) sublimates at −78 °C: it never becomes a puddle.. Snow can slowly disappear on cold, sunny, dry days without melting.

clips.send: Temperature. How fast the particles move on average. Temperature measures the average kinetic energy (motion energy) of the particles. Hotter equals particles move faster. Colder equals particles move slower. At absolute zero ( minus 273 degrees Celsius ) particle motion is at its lowest possible level.
clips.text: Temperature. How fast the particles move on average. Temperature measures the average kinetic energy (motion energy) of the particles.. Hotter = particles move faster. Colder = particles move slower.. At absolute zero (−273 °C) particle motion is at its lowest possible level.

clips.send: Liquid. Fixed volume, takes the shape of its container. Particles are still close together but can slide past one another. That is why liquids flow and can be poured. Water is unusual: liquid water is denser than ice, so ice floats.
clips.text: Liquid. Fixed volume, takes the shape of its container. Particles are still close together but can slide past one another.. That is why liquids flow and can be poured.. Water is unusual: liquid water is denser than ice, so ice floats.

clips.send: Gas. No fixed shape or volume: fills its container. Particles are far apart and move fast in straight lines until they hit something. Attractions between them are very weak. Because there is so much empty space, gases can be squeezed (compressed).
clips.text: Gas. No fixed shape or volume: fills its container. Particles are far apart and move fast in straight lines until they hit something.. Attractions between them are very weak.. Because there is so much empty space, gases can be squeezed (compressed).

clips.send: Plasma. Super-hot, electrically charged gas. At extremely high temperatures, electrons are stripped off atoms, leaving charged ions and free electrons. Plasma glows and conducts electricity: lightning, the Sun, neon signs and auroras. Most of the visible matter in the universe (stars!) is plasma.
clips.text: Plasma. Super-hot, electrically charged gas. At extremely high temperatures, electrons are stripped off atoms, leaving charged ions and free electrons.. Plasma glows and conducts electricity: lightning, the Sun, neon signs and auroras.. Most of the visible matter in the universe (stars!) is plasma.

clips.send: Deposition. Gas, solid, skipping the liquid (heat is released). Gas particles lose energy and lock straight into a solid. Frost on a cold window and snowflakes form by deposition. It is the reverse of sublimation.
clips.text: Deposition. Gas → solid, skipping the liquid (heat is released). Gas particles lose energy and lock straight into a solid.. Frost on a cold window and snowflakes form by deposition.. It is the reverse of sublimation.

clips.send: Freezing. Liquid, solid (heat is released). Water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius , the same temperature at which ice melts. Particles slow down until attractions lock them into a lattice. Freezing releases heat. Farmers spray water on fruit trees on frosty nights so the freezing water protects the fruit.
clips.text: Freezing. Liquid → solid (heat is released). Water freezes at 0 °C, the same temperature at which ice melts.. Particles slow down until attractions lock them into a lattice.. Freezing releases heat. Farmers spray water on fruit trees on frosty nights so the freezing water protects the fruit.

clips.send: Water molecule (H2O). The tiny particle that makes up water. All matter is made of tiny particles (atoms or molecules) that are always moving. Each water molecule is 1 oxygen atom (red) joined to 2 hydrogen atoms (white). Ice, liquid water and steam are made of exactly the same molecules. Only their spacing and motion change.
clips.text: Water molecule (H₂O). The tiny particle that makes up water. All matter is made of tiny particles (atoms or molecules) that are always moving.. Each water molecule is 1 oxygen atom (red) joined to 2 hydrogen atoms (white).. Ice, liquid water and steam are made of exactly the same molecules. Only their spacing and motion change.

clips.send: Solid. Fixed shape and fixed volume. Particles are packed tightly in a regular pattern (a lattice). They cannot move past each other. They only vibrate in place. Strong attractions hold the particles together.
clips.text: Solid. Fixed shape and fixed volume. Particles are packed tightly in a regular pattern (a lattice).. They cannot move past each other. They only vibrate in place.. Strong attractions hold the particles together.

clips.send: Condensation. Gas, liquid (heat is released). When water vapor cools, the molecules slow down and cling together into droplets. Examples: dew on grass, a foggy bathroom mirror, clouds. The “sweat” on a cold glass is water vapor from the air condensing, not water leaking through.
clips.text: Condensation. Gas → liquid (heat is released). When water vapor cools, the molecules slow down and cling together into droplets.. Examples: dew on grass, a foggy bathroom mirror, clouds.. The “sweat” on a cold glass is water vapor from the air condensing, not water leaking through.

clips.send: Vaporization (boiling and evaporation). Liquid, gas (heat is absorbed). Evaporation happens only at the surface and at any temperature. That is how puddles dry up. Boiling happens throughout the liquid at the boiling point: 100 degrees Celsius for water at sea level. Boiling 1 g of water takes 2260 J, almost 7 times more than melting it!
clips.text: Vaporization (boiling & evaporation). Liquid → gas (heat is absorbed). Evaporation happens only at the surface and at any temperature. That is how puddles dry up.. Boiling happens throughout the liquid at the boiling point: 100 °C for water at sea level.. Boiling 1 g of water takes 2260 J, almost 7 times more than melting it!

clips.send: 液体。体积固定，形状随容器改变。粒子仍然靠得很近，但可以相互滑动。所以液体能流动，可以倾倒。水很特别：液态水的密度比冰大，所以冰会浮在水面上。
clips.text: 液体. 体积固定，形状随容器改变. 粒子仍然靠得很近，但可以相互滑动。. 所以液体能流动，可以倾倒。. 水很特别：液态水的密度比冰大，所以冰会浮在水面上。

clips.send: 固体。有固定的形状和体积。粒子紧密地按规则的方式排列（晶格）。粒子不能相互移动位置，只能在原地振动。粒子之间有很强的吸引力，把它们束缚在一起。
clips.text: 固体. 有固定的形状和体积. 粒子紧密地按规则的方式排列（晶格）。. 粒子不能相互移动位置，只能在原地振动。. 粒子之间有很强的吸引力，把它们束缚在一起。

clips.send: 汽化（沸腾和蒸发）。液态，气态（吸收热量）。蒸发只发生在液体表面，在任何温度下都能进行，水坑就是这样变干的。沸腾在液体内部和表面同时发生，只在沸点进行：海平面上水的沸点是 100 摄氏度 。让 1 g 水沸腾汽化需要 2260 J，几乎是熔化所需能量的 7 倍！
clips.text: 汽化（沸腾和蒸发）. 液态 → 气态（吸收热量）. 蒸发只发生在液体表面，在任何温度下都能进行，水坑就是这样变干的。. 沸腾在液体内部和表面同时发生，只在沸点进行：海平面上水的沸点是 100 °C。. 让 1 g 水沸腾汽化需要 2260 J，几乎是熔化所需能量的 7 倍！

clips.send: 凝固。液态，固态（放出热量）。水在 0 摄氏度 凝固，和冰熔化的温度相同。粒子运动变慢，直到吸引力把它们锁进晶格中。凝固会放出热量。果农在霜冻的夜晚给果树喷水，水凝固时放出的热量可以保护果实。
clips.text: 凝固. 液态 → 固态（放出热量）. 水在 0 °C 凝固，和冰熔化的温度相同。. 粒子运动变慢，直到吸引力把它们锁进晶格中。. 凝固会放出热量。果农在霜冻的夜晚给果树喷水，水凝固时放出的热量可以保护果实。

clips.send: 气体。没有固定的形状和体积，会充满整个容器。粒子相距很远，沿直线高速运动，直到撞上别的东西。粒子之间的吸引力非常弱。因为粒子之间有大量空隙，气体可以被压缩。
clips.text: 气体. 没有固定的形状和体积，会充满整个容器. 粒子相距很远，沿直线高速运动，直到撞上别的东西。. 粒子之间的吸引力非常弱。. 因为粒子之间有大量空隙，气体可以被压缩。

clips.send: 凝华。气态直接变成固态（放出热量）。气体粒子失去能量，直接锁进固体中。寒冷窗户上的霜和雪花都是凝华形成的。它是升华的逆过程。
clips.text: 凝华. 气态直接变成固态（放出热量）. 气体粒子失去能量，直接锁进固体中。. 寒冷窗户上的霜和雪花都是凝华形成的。. 它是升华的逆过程。

clips.send: 液化。气态，液态（放出热量）。水蒸气遇冷时，分子运动变慢，聚集成小水滴。例子：草叶上的露水、浴室里起雾的镜子、云。冰饮料杯外壁的“汗珠”是空气中的水蒸气液化形成的，不是杯里的水渗出来的。
clips.text: 液化. 气态 → 液态（放出热量）. 水蒸气遇冷时，分子运动变慢，聚集成小水滴。. 例子：草叶上的露水、浴室里起雾的镜子、云。. 冰饮料杯外壁的“汗珠”是空气中的水蒸气液化形成的，不是杯里的水渗出来的。

clips.send: 等离子体。超高温、带电的气体。在极高的温度下，电子从原子上脱离，形成带电的离子和自由电子。等离子体会发光、能导电：闪电、太阳、霓虹灯和极光都是等离子体。宇宙中可见物质的大部分（恒星！）都是等离子体。
clips.text: 等离子体. 超高温、带电的气体. 在极高的温度下，电子从原子上脱离，形成带电的离子和自由电子。. 等离子体会发光、能导电：闪电、太阳、霓虹灯和极光都是等离子体。. 宇宙中可见物质的大部分（恒星！）都是等离子体。

clips.send: 温度。粒子平均运动的快慢。温度反映粒子的平均动能（运动的能量）。温度越高，粒子运动越快；温度越低，粒子运动越慢。在绝对零度（减273 摄氏度 ）时，粒子的运动达到最低限度。
clips.text: 温度. 粒子平均运动的快慢. 温度反映粒子的平均动能（运动的能量）。. 温度越高，粒子运动越快；温度越低，粒子运动越慢。. 在绝对零度（−273 °C）时，粒子的运动达到最低限度。

clips.send: 熔化。固态，液态（吸收热量）。冰在 0 摄氏度 熔化，这是它的熔点。熔化过程中温度保持在 0 摄氏度 ，直到冰全部熔化。吸收的能量用来拆开晶格。熔化 1 g 冰需要 334 J 的能量。
clips.text: 熔化. 固态 → 液态（吸收热量）. 冰在 0 °C 熔化，这是它的熔点。. 熔化过程中温度保持在 0 °C，直到冰全部熔化。吸收的能量用来拆开晶格。. 熔化 1 g 冰需要 334 J 的能量。

clips.send: 水分子（H2O）。构成水的微小粒子。所有物质都由不停运动的微小粒子（原子或分子）构成。每个水分子由 1 个氧原子（红色）和 2 个氢原子（白色）构成。冰、水和水蒸气由完全相同的分子构成，改变的只是分子的间距和运动方式。
clips.text: 水分子（H₂O）. 构成水的微小粒子. 所有物质都由不停运动的微小粒子（原子或分子）构成。. 每个水分子由 1 个氧原子（红色）和 2 个氢原子（白色）构成。. 冰、水和水蒸气由完全相同的分子构成，改变的只是分子的间距和运动方式。

clips.send: 升华。固态直接变成气态（吸收热量）。固体表面的粒子直接“逃”成气体。干冰（固态二氧化碳）在减78 摄氏度 升华，不会化成一滩液体。在寒冷、晴朗、干燥的日子里，积雪不经熔化也会慢慢消失。
clips.text: 升华. 固态直接变成气态（吸收热量）. 固体表面的粒子直接“逃”成气体。. 干冰（固态二氧化碳）在 −78 °C 升华，不会化成一滩液体。. 在寒冷、晴朗、干燥的日子里，积雪不经熔化也会慢慢消失。
